arxiv-2109-13885.title: Turning old models fashion again: Recycling classical CNN networks using the Lattice Transformation
arxiv-2109-13885.creator: Ana Paula G. S. de Almeida, Flavio de Barros Vidal
arxiv-2109-13885.description: Abstract In the early 1990s, the first signs of life of the CNN era were given: LeCun et al. [ 1 ] proposed a CNN model trained by the backpropagation algorithm to classify low-resolution images of handwritten digits. Undoubtedly, it was a breakthrough in the field of computer vision.

arxiv-2209-13653.title: A two-component vector WIMP – fermion FIMP dark matter model with an extended seesaw mechanism
arxiv-2209-13653.creator: Francesco Costa, Sarif Khan, and Jinsu Kim*]Corresponding author
arxiv-2209-13653.description: Abstract We consider an extension of the Standard Model that explains the neutrino masses and has a rich dark matter phenomenology. The model has two dark matter candidates, a vector WIMP and a fermion FIMP, and the sum of their relic densities matches the total dark matter abundance.

arxiv-2212-09764.title: Updated constraints on axion-like particles from temporal information in supernova SN1987A gamma-ray data
arxiv-2212-09764.creator: & Lena Schulz
arxiv-2212-09764.description: Abstract We revise gamma-ray limits on axion-like particles (ALPs) emitted from supernova SN1987A based on Solar Maximum Mission data. We improve and simplify the computation of the expected gamma-ray signal from ALP decays, while also extending it to non-instantaneous ALP emission.

arxiv-2307-15384.title: Gauss-Bonnet solution with a cloud of strings in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space
arxiv-2307-15384.creator: Wenxi Zhai, Xiangdong Zhang
arxiv-2307-15384.description: Abstract In this paper, we present exact spherically symmetric Gauss-Bonnet black hole solutions surrounded by a cloud of strings fluid with cosmological constant in D > 4 D>4 dimensions. Both charged and uncharged cases are considered. We focus on the de Sitter solutions in the main text and leave the Anti-de Sitter solutions in the appendix.

arxiv-2404-03721.title: New semicoherent targeted search for continuous gravitational waves from pulsars in binary systems
arxiv-2404-03721.creator: L. Mirasola, P. Leaci, P. Astone, L. D’Onofrio, S. Dall’Osso, A. De Falco, M. Lai, S. Mastrogiovanni, C. Palomba, A. Riggio, A. Sanna
arxiv-2404-03721.description: Abstract We present a novel semicoherent targeted search method for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) emitted by pulsars in binary systems. The method is based on a custom optimization of the coherence time, which is tailored according to the orbital parameters and their uncertainties, as provided by electromagnetic observations.

arxiv-2405-09627.title: Quantum Geometry and Stabilization of Fractional Chern Insulators Far from the Ideal Limit
arxiv-2405-09627.creator: Gal Shavit, Yuval Oreg
arxiv-2405-09627.description: Abstract In the presence of strong electronic interactions, a partially filled Chern band may stabilize a fractional Chern insulator (FCI) state, the zero-field analog of the fractional quantum Hall phase. While FCIs have long been hypothesized, feasible solid-state realizations only recently emerged, largely due to the rise of moiré materials.

pmc-11330491.title: An efficient colorectal cancer detection network using atrous convolution with coordinate attention transformer and histopathological images
pmc-11330491.creator: Majdi Khalid, Sugitha Deivasigamani, Sathiya V, Surendran Rajendran
pmc-11330491.description: The second most common type of malignant tumor worldwide is colorectal cancer. Histopathology image analysis offers crucial data for the clinical diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Currently, deep learning techniques are applied to enhance cancer classification and tumor localization in histopathological image analysis.

pmc-11512556.title: Causal Associations Between Sleep Traits and Low Grip Strength: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11512556.creator: Yihong Tai, Haonan Wang, Yinghong Dai, Liang Yu
pmc-11512556.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundSleep disorders and low grip strength often co-occur clinically and are geriatric symptoms that cause significant socioeconomic burden. Previous observational studies have found an association between sleep behaviors and grip strength, but the causal relationship remains unclear.PurposeWith the Mendelian randomization (MR) approach, the study aimed to determine the causal association between sleep traits (sleep duration, insomnia, daytime napping, sleep-wake disorders, chronotype) and low grip strength.MethodsThe study used genetic variants from the genome-wide association study (GWAS) archived in UK Biobank and FinnGen.

pmc-11670539.title: Psychological aspects in young people with venous thromboembolic disease, preliminary report
pmc-11670539.creator: Alejandro Godoy, N Bula Galli, Aldo Tabares
pmc-11670539.description: BackgroundThe decline in the mental well-being of young adults following an episode of venous thromboembolism may be related to the uncertainty of long-term health and fear of recurrence. In recent years, post-pulmonary embolism syndrome has gained acceptance, however, less attention has been given to the psychological impact on young patients after venous thromboembolism.

pmc-12649114.title: Nrf2 Activated by PD-MSCs Attenuates Oxidative Stress in a Hydrogen Peroxide-Injured Retinal Pigment Epithelial Cell Line
pmc-12649114.creator: Se Jin Hong, Dae-Hyun Lee, Jeong Woo Choi, Hankyu Lee, Youngje Sung, Gi Jin Kim, Paola Irato
pmc-12649114.description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a retinal degenerative disease caused by oxidative stress. Thus, we aimed to reduce oxidative stress through the use of placenta-derived mesenchymal stem cells (PD-MSCs). To induce oxidative stress in ARPE-19 cells, we treated them with 200 µM hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) for 2 h and then cocultured them with PD-MSCs.

pmc-13225391.title: Establishment and application of a quadruple target real-time PCR assay for detecting Yersinia pestis
pmc-13225391.creator: Wenfang Wang, Xiaoxue Zhang, Hui Yu, Zhanli Wang
pmc-13225391.description: In order to establish an efficient method for high-throughput detection of Yersinia pestis (Y. pestis), a quadruple target real-time polymerase chain reaction assay was developed based on the specific target genes of Y. pestis (caf1, pla, ymt, and ypo-1094). Its sensitivity, specificity, and repeatability were evaluated, and clinical serum samples were tested by the established method.

pmc-13418106.title: Game-Theoretic Optimized Federated Learning for Heterogeneous IoT Object Detection
pmc-13418106.creator: Zepeng Wang, Jie Chen
pmc-13418106.description: Federated object detection allows distributed IoT cameras to learn a shared detector without exposing raw images. Its performance is limited by non-IID scenes, unequal device resources, intermittent links, and selfish participation. We propose GO-FedDet, a game-theoretic optimized federated detection framework for heterogeneous IoT application.

pmc-13426011.title: Mito‐Nuclear Discordance and Species Boundaries in the Freshwater Fish Genus Cyprinion Revealed by Genome‐Wide SNPs
pmc-13426011.creator: Iraj Hashemzadeh Segherloo, Matthias F Geiger, Eric Normandeau, Jörg Freyhof
pmc-13426011.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The cyprinid genus Cyprinion, comprising nine species distributed from the Indus drainage across the Iranian Plateau to Mesopotamia and the Arabian Peninsula, exhibits contentious species boundaries due to extensive morphological overlap and limited molecular data. In this study, we integrated mitochondrial DNA (COI) sequences and genome‐wide single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data to investigate the phylogenetic relationships, taxonomy, and biogeography of six species: C. Mitochondrial analyses revealed extremely shallow divergence among C. tenuiradius , sharing identical or closely related haplotypes.

pmc-13464462.title: Trust in federal statistical agencies and vaccine uptake among U.S. adults
pmc-13464462.creator: Nathaniel J Maxey, Jemar R Bather, Taliyah S Griffin, Plamena P Powla, Felix M Pabon-Rodriguez
pmc-13464462.description: Background:In the United States (US), COVID-19 vaccination saved 3.2 million lives from 2020 to 2023, yet vaccine uptake remains a public health challenge. Seasonal influenza vaccination also remains an important public health priority because influenza contributes substantially to preventable morbidity and mortality each year.

pmc-13502771.title: Mean Arterial Pressure at Admission Predicts 28-day Mortality in Patients With Severe Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis
pmc-13502771.creator: Meritxell Ventura-Cots, Ana Clemente, Edilmar Alvarado-Tapias, Sujan Ravi, Berta Cuyas, Marion Tanguy, Maria Poca, Marion Jager, Carlos Fernández-Carrillo, Gavin E. Arteel, Ares Villagrasa, Anna Aguilar-Amorós, Josepmaria Argemi, Juan G. Abraldes, Francisco Bosques, Robert S. Brown, Guadalupe Garcia
pmc-13502771.description: INTRODUCTION:Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) is a severe condition with high short-term mortality. Identifying key predictors of poor outcomes is critical for guiding therapeutic strategies. Mean arterial pressure (MAP), a key determinant of tissue perfusion and systemic hemodynamics, may play a pivotal role in prognosis.

pmc-13567626.title: Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting Flow and Consistency Retention Performance in Cementitious Mixtures with Diverse Grinding Aid Dosages and Types
pmc-13567626.creator: Yahya Kaya, Veysel Kobya, Naz Mardani, Gulveren Tabansiz-Goc, Fatih Cavdur, Ali Mardani
pmc-13567626.description: Grinding aids (GAs) are commonly utilized to enhance energy efficiency during clinker grinding and improve cement properties. However, alongside their benefits, GAs may lead to challenges such as reduced flow performance, loss of consistency retention, and increased demand for water or water-reducing admixtures in cementitious systems.

pmc-13591393.title: Inhibitory Effects of Tenebrio molitor Larva Trypsin Hydrolysate on Androgenetic Alopecia
pmc-13591393.creator: Seok-Hee Kim, Young-Jin Choi, Nishala Erandi Wedamulla, Qun Zhang, Jin-Hwan Lee, Eun-Kyung Kim
pmc-13591393.description: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common form of hair loss, with a high prevalence worldwide. In this study, we aimed to investigate the potential of Tenebrio molitor larva trypsin hydrolysate (TMTH), an insect-derived bioactive hydrolysate, as a functional ingredient candidate for AGA.
